_README: source-retention-policy.json — HOW LONG Correlix keeps a corresponding-source
artifact, and WHO decided that. Read by scripts/source-archive.py to compute the
S3 Object Lock `retain_until` stamped on every archived artifact, and by
`source-archive.py retention show` to explain each stamped date.
WHY THIS IS A FILE AND NOT A CONSTANT IN THE CODE
The retention period is a LEGAL question, not an engineering one. GPL-2.0 §3(b)
names three years for a written offer; GPL-3.0 §6(b) names three years or the
life of the product's support, whichever is longer; LGPL inherits both; and none
of that answers what a court in a given jurisdiction expects of a company that
shipped the binary. Hard-coding `end_of_support + 3y` in a script would be this
project asserting a legal conclusion it is not qualified to reach. So the number
lives here, in one owner-owned field, with the reasoning written beside it, and
the tooling only ARITHMETIC — it never invents a rule.
FAIL-CLOSED AND MONOTONIC
* Retention is only ever EXTENDED. `source-archive.py` refuses to write a
retain_until earlier than one already stamped on an object or recorded in
docs/compliance/source-archive-index.json; shortening is an Object Lock
administrative action a human performs deliberately, never a side effect of
a CI run. Ordinary CI holds no permission to do it at all (the read role has
no PutObjectRetention and no BypassGovernanceRetention).
* Editing `owner_decision.retention_years` DOWN changes nothing about already
archived objects. It changes only what future ingests stamp.
* `counsel_confirmed: false` is the honest state today. The tooling still
works — it stamps the conservative default and says so in every trace —
but no document generated from this file may claim the period is a legal
determination until that flag is true and `counsel_confirmed_by` names a
real reviewer. Never invent one.

_why: The single field a human owns. Everything else in this file is either a
derivation of it or an explanation of it.
10 years is chosen as a DELIBERATELY CONSERVATIVE default: it is longer than
GPL-2.0 §3(b)'s three years, longer than any support window Correlix has
committed to, and long enough that no ordinary release ages out of it before
counsel has looked at the question. Over-retaining source costs storage.
Under-retaining it is a licence violation that cannot be repaired after the
fact, because the bytes are gone. The asymmetry decides the default.
owner_decision.note: Conservative engineering default pending counsel. NOT a legal determination.

_why: How `retain_until` is derived, recorded per artifact so an auditor can
reproduce the date rather than trust it. The base date is the LATEST of the
inputs available at ingest time, so a later release of the same artifact can
only push the date out, never pull it in.
calculation.base_date: the latest of: the ingest date, and the distribution end date of every Correlix release that references the artifact (when known)
calculation.base_date_fallback_reason: Correlix has published no end-of-distribution dates yet, so the ingest date is used and recorded as such. When a release records an end-of-distribution date, re-running `source-archive.py ingest --extend-retention` recomputes from it and can only extend.
calculation.monotonic_note: A computed date earlier than one already stamped is DISCARDED and the existing date kept; the run reports it.

_why: Object Lock mode. GOVERNANCE while the process is being validated, so an
administrator holding s3:BypassGovernanceRetention can correct a mistake made
while the tooling is new. COMPLIANCE afterwards.
COMPLIANCE MODE IS INTENTIONALLY IMPOSSIBLE TO OVERRIDE. Under COMPLIANCE, no
principal — not the ingest role, not an administrator, not the AWS account
root user, not AWS Support — can shorten a retention period or delete a locked
object version before it expires. That is the entire point of the mode and it
is the reason the switch is a separate, deliberate, owner-authorised step
rather than a default: an object written with a wrong 10-year COMPLIANCE lock
occupies paid storage for 10 years and there is no appeal.
Switching requires: (1) the ingest/verify/release path proven end to end
against the real bucket, (2) the retention arithmetic reviewed against a
counsel-confirmed period, (3) an owner decision recorded here.
compliance_mode_preconditions: the company AWS account, bucket and roles exist and the full ingest → verify → release-fetch path has run against them
the owner records the switch in this file with a date

legal_hold.note: s3:PutObjectLegalHold is an administrator action, held by no CI role. A legal hold suspends expiry independently of retain_until and is released by a human.

_why: WHICH artifacts this policy governs. Small archives stay in git (they are
already retained, versioned and distributed with the repository); large ones
go to S3. The threshold is an operational one about git history size, not a
compliance one — both locations are Correlix-controlled retention.
scope.git_retained: compliance/corresponding-sources/ — artifacts small enough to live in git history forever
scope.archive_retained: the S3 archive — everything else with a corresponding-source obligation
scope.note: An artifact may be in BOTH. Retention in git is unbounded (history); the S3 copy carries the Object Lock stamp.
